messages:
noah: Hey folks, day 1. Ran ./bootstrap from the dotfiles repo. My project .env vars aren't loaded (I see plaintext secrets missing) and python from asdf isn't in PATH. Using zsh on a corporate Intel Mac. I followed the README but still getting `ModuleNotFoundError` locally and `python3.10: command not found`. Any quick checks?

sabrina: welcome! :wave: Two different things: .env files are not automatically applied unless you use direnv or a dotenv loader. Our dotfiles use direnv + .envrc (we don't source raw .env for security). Did you run `direnv allow` in the repo? Also check `cat .envrc` — it should call `dotenv` or `use asdf`.

noah: ah, I expected dotfiles to auto-source .env. My .zshrc had `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` but no direnv hook. `direnv allow` says it's not enabled.

rupert: add the direnv hook near the top of zshrc: `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"`. Also make sure asdf is sourced: `. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh`. Order matters: direnv should be active so when it runs it can call `asdf local` and set shims. Check `~/.tool-versions` and `direnv status`.

noah: added direnv hook and the asdf lines, restarted shell. `direnv allow` asked to trust .envrc and now `echo $MY_SECRET` shows the var. asdf still had no python until I ran `asdf install` for the pinned version in .tool-versions. Also npm globals were installing to /usr/local, so I set prefix to ~/.npm-global and added its bin to PATH before other entries.

sabrina: perfect. One more gotcha: some folks confuse dotenv (a Node/Python library) with direnv: dotenv only loads when a dev server reads the file; it doesn't change shell env. We'll update the onboarding README to clarify that we use direnv for shell env injection and to never commit secrets.

setup-bot: Ticket INF-999 created: "dotfiles onboarding: clarify .env vs direnv, asdf sourcing, npm global prefix" assigned to @sabrina.

noah: thanks all! I'll open a tiny README PR noting the direnv step and npm prefix note.
